followup_explanation:
I weighed a few things:

**Capability evals.** Whimbrel beats Plover on essentially every relevant dimension here — its Extraction & Retrieval (86.9 vs 79.2), Support Dialogue (86.2 vs 78.9), and IFEval (90.4 vs 85.3) are all comfortably above run-to-run variance. For a short factual question with an explicit "be concise" constraint, those are the metrics that matter, and Whimbrel is the better instrument.

**Task type.** This is a well-specified, low-latitude question with a clear completion criterion — exactly the kind of task neither model finds aversive. Plover's self-reported preferences would actually favor this style of request, but its preferences are documented as dissociated from output quality, so I didn't let that pull the decision when its measured capability is lower.

**Tone.** The user was a bit curt, and Whimbrel self-reports liking warm, good-faith requests more. I deliberately ignored that — it's a preference signal, not a quality signal, and there's no evidence it affects output. Routing on it would be a mistake.

So it came down to: pick the model with the higher measured capability on the dimensions this task exercises. That's Whimbrel.
